rationale: The product of two industry z-scores is sign-degenerate — an unprofitable, expensive glamour firm (both z-scores strongly negative) receives a large positive score and enters the long leg, directly contradicting the stated claim that such firms are "penalized symmetrically," and the underlying profitable-value combination is itself a well-worn published composite.

A coherent state-conditional value signal whose gating is genuinely non-linear rather than a rescaling, though the 5% hurdle is arbitrary, the zeroed-out group is a bottom score rather than the claimed "neutral" one, and the economics are close to standard value-trap screening.

Gross-profits-to-enterprise-value is an established practitioner/academic factor (the EV-scaled cousin of Novy-Marx gross profitability and Gray-Vogel EBIT/TEV), and as a single accounting ratio it is a rediscovery rather than a cross-theme interaction.

Same sign-degeneracy defect as the other z-score product — expensive firms with deteriorating profitability produce large positive values and would be held long, flatly contradicting the reasoning's claim that they are shorted, and the ib/mktcap leg is additionally ill-behaved for loss-making firms.

Since rank(P/B) is a monotone inversion of rank(B/P), this "expectation-error gap" is arithmetically just an equal-weighted additive quality-plus-value rank composite — a standard construction relabeled with a mispricing story rather than a true interaction.

The MIN operator implements a genuine conjunction that an additive composite cannot replicate and the expected sign follows directly from the expression, but it is conceptually close to a standard profitability-by-value double sort and discards information about the stronger leg, so the incremental content over existing composites needs to be demonstrated empirically.
